Detailed Description

This is a slightly modified version of the Yale Sparse Matrix Format. The typical Yale format would, in the place of double **mvec, have a double *A type and an additional array, int *IA, which stores the index into A at which row i would begin. For example, A[IA[i]] is the first non-zero entry in row i of the matrix stored in A. Instead of this, I have used a double pointer to represent variable-length rows in a matrix. It is equivalent to if not better than using the additional IA vector because it takes a tiny amount of pointer arithmetic out of the act of dereferencing a value in the matrix. The double *lvec variable is such that lvec[i] is the number of non-zero entries in row i of the matrix.
Parameters:
nvals Stores the number of non-zero entries in the matrix
nrows The number of rows
ncols The number of columns
mvec Stores the actual non-zero entries; mvec[i][j] is the value of row i, column jvec[i][j]
jvec jvec[i][j] is the column of the value stored at mvec[i][j]
lvec lvec[i] is the number of non-zero entries in row i
